calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets lot requirements for a detached house, those requirements are applied to a detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Read as INCLUDE (the houseplex takes the exception's detached-house lot requirements); a PROCEDURAL reading is possible because it opens with 'Despite regulations 900.1.10(3) and 900.1.10(4)(A)'. The condition 'the only residential building on a lot' has no vocab.lot_condition token and is not keyed as a condition. Depends on Chapter 900 exception content (backlog).

units.disclosure: If your lot is in a Chapter 900 exception area with lot requirements for a detached house, those requirements also apply to a detached houseplex; we do not yet evaluate exception lot requirements.

calculation_handling.description: Where a Chapter 900 exception sets lot requirements for a semi-detached house, those requirements (for the portion that is an individual dwelling unit) are applied to a semi-detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot.
calculation_handling.gaps: Read as INCLUDE; a PROCEDURAL reading is possible ('Despite regulations 900.1.10(3) and 900.1.10(4)(A)'). The condition 'the only residential building on a lot' has no vocab.lot_condition token. Depends on Chapter 900 exception content (backlog).

units.disclosure: If your lot is in a Chapter 900 exception area with lot requirements for a semi-detached house, those requirements also apply to a semi-detached houseplex; we do not yet evaluate exception lot requirements.

evidence.semi_detached_houseplex: semi-detached houseplex or a residential building

calculation_handling.description: Where the lot coverage under 10.10.60.70(1)(C) is more permissive than the coverage that would apply under 10.10.30.1(1) (exception lot requirements), the more permissive one prevails.
calculation_handling.gaps: Precedence is conditional on which value is more permissive, not a fixed layer order; 'base > exception' records that the base-chapter regulation 10.10.60.70(1)(C) may override the exception-derived coverage despite 900.1.10(3)/(4)(A). The secondary-suite arm is an alternative (or), not a conjunction, so it is recorded in application rather than condition.

10.10.30.1(1).explanation: If your lot is covered by a site-specific Chapter 900 exception that sets lot requirements for a detached or semi-detached house, a detached or semi-detached houseplex that is the only residential building on the lot must meet those same exception requirements.

10.10.30.1(2).explanation: For a houseplex or a house with a secondary suite, if the general lot coverage rule in 10.10.60.70(1)(C) is more generous than the coverage set by a site-specific exception, the more generous lot coverage applies.
